children: will be reporting earnings this Monday after the bell. Here’s what to look for.

Paymentus beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $360.7 million, up 28.8% year on year. It was an exceptional quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates and an impressive beat of analysts’ EBITDA estimates.
Is Paymentus a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Paymentus’s revenue to grow 15.5% year on year, slowing from the 34.2% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Paymentus has a history of exceeding Wall Street’s expectations.

Looking at Paymentus’s peers in the diversified financial services segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Donnelley Financial Solutions delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 5.5%, beating analysts’ expectations by 2.8%, and WEX reported revenues up 12.8%, topping estimates by 3.2%. Donnelley Financial Solutions traded up 25.9% following the results while WEX was down 3.3%.

There has been positive sentiment among investors in the diversified financial services segment, with share prices up 4.1% on average over the last month. Paymentus is up 6.5% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $40.14 (compared to the current share price of $32.85).
